title: A 24-winter ENSO test detected an 8.8% simulated error gain in only 13% of fixed-design trials
abstract: We tested the sensitivity of a published spring ocean volume forecast comparison. We held its 43 annual predictor rows fixed and simulated 1,000 target records per signal and noise case. Each record used chronological linear fits and a paired three-year block interval across 24 target winters in 2001-2024. A known volume signal with 8.8% exact expected mean squared error reduction gave detection in only 12.7-13.1% of trials. A 26.3% expected reduction gave detection in 32.2-34.4%. Zero signal gave 0.9% detection. Independent Gaussian errors and a fitted stationary AR(1) model gave similar results. Thus this short test often misses useful signals under these assumptions. This does not show that volume has a real effect or that surface history is physically redundant. Fixed predictors, Gaussian errors, full-record calibration, constant coefficients, revised data, and finite simulation counts limit the result. The package gives verified source-derived inputs, original code, all simulation scores, analytic expected errors, source hashes, a figure, and repeat instructions.
